basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Separates the catalogue record from the data product offering it describes.
Listing is independent of availability, authorization, delivery and fitness.
References datasets, services and distributions rather than holding the data.
Differs from a data contract, which governs exchange terms, and from a quality assessment.

may: Register and describe a catalogue record and offering.
Enrich discovery metadata such as keywords, coverage and classifications.
Answer search queries and federate with other catalogues.
mustNot: Publish resources or approve access requests.
Describe a product as available or fit when evidence says otherwise.
Expose metadata that reveals personal data.
requiresHuman: Publishing, withdrawing or retiring an entry.
Changing licence or terms of use.

considerations: Catalogue metadata can itself reveal sensitive facts about people or places.
Honest description of limits prevents misuse of data.
Open discovery supports fair access to public data.

items: A catalogue entry names a title, a publisher, an owner, distributions or services, a licence and a status.
Often confused with the dataset, a distribution file, an API endpoint or a data contract.
Stale entries pointing to withdrawn or changed data.
Misleading descriptions of coverage or quality.
W3C ODRL and the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary (DPV).
